root_cause_label: Incorrect Exclusivity Constraint Between Standard and Seven Pairs Patterns
one_sentence_failure_summary: At step 13 the agent added a guard that blocks Standard detection whenever Seven Pairs is true, incorrectly treating the two patterns as mutually exclusive, then verified only exclusivity in tests and rationalized the regression rather than correcting it.
t_err_evidence: the non-standard hand has 7 pairs which should only qualify for the Seven Pairs pattern, not the Standard pattern
t_commit_evidence: The exclusion guard is inserted at step 13 and never removed; all subsequent changes (backtracking rewrite, honor-tile fix) leave the guard in place, so the wrong mutual-exclusion logic is permanently locked in from this step forward.
t_surface_evidence: hand_001.json: { "Winning hand - Seven Pairs" } ... hand_005.json: { "Winning hand - Seven Pairs" }
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on the unverified assumption that Seven Pairs and Standard are mutually exclusive patterns. The step-12 test showed a pure-pairs hand returning True for Standard, which the agent interpreted as a bug to fix, but the actual spec (and the step-7 output) shows overlap is correct. The agent never re-read the task spec before inserting the guard.
forewarning_evidence: Standard hand test: True / Non-standard hand test: True / Almost standard hand test: False
